claims.text: High-temperature oxidation resistance and material integrity in the proposed MPEA are governed by the combination of a refined eutectic microstructure and lattice-distortion-induced diffusion suppression.
A refined lamellar eutectic microstructure promotes rapid formation of a protective Al2O3 scale during initial oxidation.
The initially formed Al2O3 scale is selective and exclusive.
Lattice distortion in the Al-depletion zone elevates vacancy formation energies.
Lattice distortion increases Al migration barriers in the Al-depletion zone.
The elevated vacancy-formation and Al-migration barriers suppress continued Al diffusion toward the oxidation front.
Diffusion suppression slows sustained thermally grown oxide growth.
The combined microstructural and diffusion-suppression mechanism reduces oxide-scale spallation.
A Y- and Hf-co-doped NiCoCrAl-type MPEA can exhibit a significantly refined eutectic structure and pronounced lattice distortion.
The refined lamellar structure lowers the critical Al concentration required for exclusive Al2O3 formation.
Relative to a typical NiCoCrAlY alloy, the engineered MPEA should reduce TGO growth rate by roughly 50–60% at 1200°C.
The engineered MPEA should exhibit enhanced spallation resistance over 500 hours at 1200°C.
The conventional baseline will exhibit faster oxide growth than the engineered MPEA.
The conventional baseline will exhibit more frequent spallation events than the engineered MPEA.
The proposed controlled comparison uses oxidation at approximately 1200°C for 500 hours under matched oxygen partial pressure and thermal conditions.
The mechanism is expected to dominate in Al-containing high-entropy or multiprincipal-element alloys oxidized at approximately 1200°C.
The mechanism may not apply to substantially different alloy compositions or substantially lower oxidation temperatures.
Initial oxidation behavior in complex multielement alloys depends on elemental interactions, atomic size, redox potential, and thermodynamics.
